The 2026 UEFA Champions League Final is heading to Budapest, Hungary, where Puskás Aréna will host the biggest match in European club football.

Opened in 2019, the stadium was built on the site of Hungary’s former national ground and named after football legend Ferenc Puskás. With a capacity of around 67,000, modern infrastructure, and UEFA elite status, the venue has quickly become one of Central Europe’s most important football stadiums.

Budapest has already hosted major tournaments, including matches during UEFA Euro 2020 and the 2023 Europa League Final. Now the city will stage the Champions League Final for the first time — bringing one of the most watched sporting events in the world to Hungary.

In this video we break down the stadium, its history, why Budapest was chosen, and what to expect when Europe’s biggest clubs arrive for the 2026 final.
